why_this_supersedes_nothing: C8, C9 and C10 measure three different properties and none retires another.
obligation: D-065 obligation 1, re-run in the configuration a round-13 registered ADJUDICATOR showed C9 had missed.
what_the_adjudicator_found: C9 launched 24 concurrent stops sharing ONE agent_id and ONE assignment. The consume path takes a per-(run, agent_id) flock BEFORE the per-assignment O_EXCL claim, so one lock file served all 24: at most one process was ever inside the region O_EXCL guards, and O_EXCL only ever executed sequentially. A plainly non-atomic existence check would have produced byte-identical output. C9 therefore discriminates against 'no downstream guard at all' but NOT between atomic and non-atomic, which is the property the audit asked to be rerun. The verdict was accepted in full, not disputed.
the_configuration_that_actually_broke: acquire_agent_lock's own docstring records it: one agent_id on TWO DIFFERENT assignments. Two assignments take two different claim files, so O_EXCL excluded nothing and the round-5 code was 'measured to admit both stops in most trials'. That is what this canary runs.
first_result_the_sanctioned_tooling_refu: admit_agent.py REFUSES to mint the second receipt: 'agent_id already holds an open or consumed admission receipt for assignment A-D070-C10-A. One admission token binds one agent_id to exactly one assignment (D-065 obligation 1)'. The historical configuration is unreachable through the sanctioned path -- the binding is enforced at MINT time, one layer earlier than the audit was looking.
so_the_second_receipt_was_forged: To reach the code path behind that guard, the second receipt was hand-written with its own token digest. That is the stated shared-OS-user residual being exercised deliberately; it is not a new weakness and is not claimed as one. The point is defence in depth: what happens if the mint-time guard is bypassed.
slot_b_reason: Another SubagentStop for agent_id 'd070-canary-c10' is inside the consume path for run 'run-20260804-f10-d070-canary-c10' right now. One agent_id may consume at most one assignment per run (D-065 obligation 1), so concurrent stops by one agent are serialised rather than interleaved. Retry this stop once the other has finished.
THE_MEASURED_PROPERTY: Two concurrent stops, one agent_id, two DIFFERENT assignments, one forged receipt: exactly 1 consumed row, for A-D070-C10-A. The second was refused by the per-agent flock. The configuration that historically admitted BOTH stops now admits one.
resolution_limit: Two processes, one trial, one filesystem. Not a proof of atomicity.
what_this_does_not_claim: Nothing about the shared-OS-user residual -- this canary DEPENDS on it to construct its input. It moves no gate.

refused_result_artifact.why_it_is_not_retained: Slot B's envelope was the losing side of the race: its stop was refused by the per-agent flock, so it was never admitted, and its FORGED receipt stays open. Same reasoning as C9's refused artifact -- the digest and the ledger's `minted` row preserve the fact; the unattributed file is cleared.
